rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spending includes obligatory and voluntary gifts for every good cause, not only a single form of charity.
rows.anchor: gerek farz ve vâcib ve gerek nâfile ve tetavvu‘olsun hayr ü hasenâta bezl-i emvâl eyleyenlerin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The seed's seven ears, each with a hundred grains, picture a seven-hundredfold return; believers should not dismiss even one grain or fear spending it.
rows.anchor: Mü’minler bir dâneyi bile küçük görmemeli, telef etmemeli ve Allah’tan hiçbir şey kıskanmamalıdır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Divine wisdom makes a seed sprout and multiply; without that order it would rot, so human deeds too can multiply through God's wisdom.
rows.anchor: Nizâm-ı hikmet ve sırr-ı ba‘s olmasa idi o bir dâne çürür gider, ne filiz verirdi ne başak.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending in God's path will take increasingly multiplied forms in the afterlife and be placed on the balance.
rows.anchor: Fî-sebîlillâh yapılan infaklar dahi âhirette böyle inkişâfât-ı mütezâyide ile temessül edecek ve mîzâna konacaktır.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author's example extends the seed's multiplication to human action: a single grain can produce hundreds through God's wisdom.
rows.anchor: İşte ef‘âl-i ‘ibâd da böyledir. Böyle [898] olduğu içindir ki

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because habba can mean any seed, some crops visibly demonstrate the parable's increase, though comparable wheat yields are said to be rare.
rows.anchor: habbe ne cinsten olursa olsun herhangi bir dâneye ıtlak edildiğine göre mahsuldar tarlalara ekilen kum darı gibi bazı hubûbâtta bu feyz meşhûdâttandır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if such a yield is rare, the verse indicates that divine wisdom permits it at minimum; inadequate cultivation explains why it is not achieved.
rows.anchor: hikmet-i ilâhiye asgarî olmak üzere bu kadarına müsâiddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Improved agriculture and removal of corruption could attain such yields, ending disputes and despair about insufficient earthly provisions.
rows.anchor: insanlar fesâdı bertaraf edip ilm-i zirâati de terakki ettirecek olurlarsa bu kadar mahsul almaya mübeşşerdirler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The intended lesson is to spend the crop for God's path, not to accumulate grain; its true harvest comes in Paradise.
rows.anchor: Maksad buğday toplamak değil onları yerinde fî-sebîlillâh sarf etmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promised return is at least seven hundredfold and may multiply further without limit.
rows.anchor: bire yedi yüzden aşağısı yok

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In al-Bazzi's reading from Ibn Kathir, the verb is read yuda'ifu, with the same meaning.
rows.anchor: İbn Kesîr’den Bezzî kıraatinde يُضَٰعِفُ okunur ki mâna bir demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Agricultural experiments are said to yield over two thousand grains from one wheat grain by separating and replanting its shoots.
rows.anchor: bir buğday dânesinden çıkan çimleri çatallandıktan sonra ayırarak fide hâlinde dikmek suretiyle bir dâneden iki bin dâneyi mütecâviz hâsılat alınabildiğini müşahede etmişlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Life's laws work by multiplication, so spending for people's benefit, God's word, and especially the fighters brings unbounded reward with God.
rows.anchor: hayatta erbâb-ı hayâtın intifâ‘ı ve kelimetullâhın i‘lâsı için fî-sebîlillâh Allah’ın kullarına ve ‘ale’l-husûs mücâhidîne bezl edilen infâkāt ü sadakātın ‘indallah nâmütenâhî semerât ü sevâba sebep olacağı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's vast mercy is not exhausted by abundant spending, and His knowledge accurately encompasses each donor's intention, amount, and promised return.
rows.anchor: infak edenin niyetini, mikdâr-ı infâkını, hâsılât-ı mev‘ûdesini bilir, hiçbirinin hesâbını şaşırmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sebilullah means God's path or religion; in legal usage it is more commonly associated with jihad because jihad protects religion and believers from coercion.
rows.anchor: “Sebîlullâh”; Allah yolu, din demektir. Fakat dinin damânı ve ehl-i dinin ikrahtan vikāyesi demek olan cihâd fî-sebîlillâh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some exegetes restrict this verse to fighters who spend their own wealth and the next verse to those who fund other fighters, assigning jihad at least seven hundred against ten for other good deeds.
rows.anchor: bu âyet bizzat cihâda giden ve kendi emvâlini sarf eden mücâhidîne, bundan sonraki de kendi gitmeyerek diğer mücâhidîne infak yapanlar hakkında nâzil olmuştur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preferred view treats ten as the minimum for all good deeds and this verse as general encouragement to spend in every good cause; the next verse explains acceptance conditions.
rows.anchor: bire on ‘ale’l-‘umûm hasenâtın hadd-i asgarîsi olup, cihad ve diğer bazı a‘mâl gibi infak başkaca meziyeti hâiz olduğundan bu âyet ‘ale’l-‘umûm infâka tergīb

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Umar reports that after this verse was revealed, the Prophet prayed for a greater reward for his community, after which 39:10 was revealed.
rows.anchor: Tefsîr-i Ebî Hayyân’da İbn Ömer’den mervîdir ki bu âyet nâzil olduğu zaman Resûlullah

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Spending's reward is not automatic: only those who do not follow their gifts with reminders or hurt receive the promised reward with their Lord and have no fear or grief.
rows.anchor: sonra da infaklarına ne minnet ne ezâ takıştırmayanlar, mağrurlanmayan, tiksindirmeyenlerdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those donors fear only God and expect reward only from Him, so they have no other fear or grief and receive multiplied recompense for what they lose.
rows.anchor: yalnız Allah’tan korkup ve ancak O’ndan ecir beklediklerinden dolayı bunlara ne başka bir korku gelir, ne de mahzun olurlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omission of fa avoids suggesting that spending itself is the true, sufficient cause of reward; God remains the real cause and acceptance depends on His conditions.
rows.anchor: asıl sebeb-i hakīkīnin Allah olduğunu ve hikmetin izzet-i ilâhiyeyi selb etmeyeceğini ifham

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Minnet has two lexical senses: favor or blessing, and diminishing a gift by counting it or taking pride in it; the latter is intended here.
rows.anchor: Diğeri de bir hakkı tenkīs etmek, kesmek, ezcümle ihsan ettiği kimseye karşı ihsânını bir şey saymak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ezā includes making a recipient recoil, complaining over a fault because of one's gift, insulting them, and throwing the gift in their face; Turkish minnet can cover both terms.
rows.anchor: in‘âmı yüzüne vurmak, başa kakmak hep ezâdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One should do good as a duty and forget it, since reward depends on intention; the Creator knows even when the recipient does not.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı iyiliği bir vazife diye yapmalı ve unutmalı. Yaptığı bir iyiliğe göz dikmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Uthman gave a thousand camels with their equipment and Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf gave four thousand dirhams to equip the Tabuk hardship army, and this verse was revealed in their honor.
rows.anchor: Gazve-i Tebük için ihzar olunan ve “Ceyş-i ‘usret” tesmiye edilen ordunun techîzine Hazret-i Osman

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rule of the verse is general and not confined to the reported occasion of revelation.
rows.anchor: Hükmün sebeb-i nüzûle mahsus olmadığı da mâlumdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A kind word that gently refuses, together with overlooking faults and answering impropriety with forgiveness, is better than charity followed by hurt.
rows.anchor: gönül alan hoş bir söz, tatlı dille reddetmek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is self-sufficient and does not make the poor bear another person's burden of gratitude; He may provide unexpectedly until the poor can give to their former benefactor.
rows.anchor: Ganî olan Allah fukarâsını başkalarının bâr-ı minnetine tahammül ettirmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is forbearing and delays punishment so sinners, including those who hurt recipients, may repent; the delay does not mean they deserve no punishment.
rows.anchor: Ezâ yapanları da ukūbete müstahik olmadıklarından dolayı değil, fakat tevbekâr olsunlar diye hilminden dolayı imhal eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Believers are warned not to nullify charity by reminding recipients or hurting them, since either behavior removes its reward.
rows.anchor: sadakalarınızı yüze vurmak, başa kakmakla ibtal etmeyiniz, bunlardan biriyle ecrini kesmeyiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The insincere donor resembles a bare rock thinly covered with soil: a downpour strips it clean, leaving the apparent planting fruitless.
rows.anchor: cascavlak bırakmış, bir toz bile kalmamış yalçın kayanın bu hâli gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The showoff who lacks belief in God and the Last Day gains nothing from the deed, just as charity poisoned by reminders or hurt earns nothing.
rows.anchor: imansızlıkla infak, riyâ ile, menn ü ezâ ile sadaka verenler kesb ettikleri bu amelden hiçbir şey elde edemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not guide the disbelieving people to good; believers who make their charity like disbelievers' ostentatious spending also lose their reward.
rows.anchor: sadakalarını menn ü ezâ ile kâfirlerin mürâiyâne sarfiyâtına benzeten mü’minler de onlar gibi ecirden mahrum kalırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sincere donor seeks God's pleasure and uses wealth to steady themselves, their deeds, and their companions against corrupt inclinations and instability, making good works a settled habit.
rows.anchor: hayr ü hasenâtı kendilerine meleke-i sâbite kılmak ve ondan sonra her nevi fezâil ve ibâdâtı suhûletle yapmak

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A garden on a high hill yields twice its usual fruit under a heavy rain; the earlier rain that stripped rock becomes mercy here.
rows.anchor: O kayayı cascavlak bırakan yağmur, bu tepede ‘ayn-ı rahmet olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The garden's doubled yield does not reduce the earlier promise of seven hundredfold; it adds another multiplication.
rows.anchor: Bu temsil bâlâdaki bire yedi yüz ve daha kat kat vaadini tenzil etmiş değil, belki bir daha katlamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even without a heavy downpour, a light drizzle or slight moisture is enough for the garden to produce its yield.
rows.anchor: hafif bir yağmur, az bir nem de yetişir, vereceğini yine verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because God sees and knows deeds, donors must avoid showing off and remain sincere in private and public.
rows.anchor: Sakın gösteriş yapmayın, gizlide âşikârda ihlâstan ayrılmayın

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The image asks whether anyone would want a rich orchard to burn just when old age and helpless young dependents make its loss devastating.
rows.anchor: ve bu hâlde elleri ermez, güçleri yetmez yavrucukları dahi bulunsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Faith and good deeds are like gardens whose reward is destroyed at Judgment by disbelief, ostentation, reminders, hurt, and other corrupt motives.
rows.anchor: imansızlık, riyâ, menn ü ezâ ve sâir ağrâz-ı fâside gibi seyyiât da yevm-i kıyâmette o ateşli bora gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Islamic polity is also a garden that prepares the way to eternal blessing; coercive, unbelieving injustice, immorality, and loss of resolve can devastate both worldly life and the afterlife.
rows.anchor: dâr-ı İslâm dahi böyle hüsn-i infak ve a‘mâl-i sâliha mahsûlü bir bağa, bir cennete

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God explains signs so people reflect, draw sound analogies from them, apply principles to their circumstances, reach conclusions, and act toward their aims.
rows.anchor: ibretler alasınız, güzel güzel kıyaslara yol bulasınız, bunların her birini delil, asıl, düstur, mebde’

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Thought is the process of arranging known matters to discover what is unknown.
rows.anchor: “fikir”, umûr-i ma‘lûmeyi tertib ile mâlumdan meçhûlü bulmaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The discussion turns toward where, how, and to whom obligatory and voluntary spending should be given.
rows.anchor: o infakları nereden yapacağız, zekâtları, sadakaları nereden ve nasıl ve kimlere vereceğiz mi diyeceksiniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two primary sources of wealth are acquisition through work and what God brings forth from the earth, including crops, fruits, minerals, and buried treasure.
rows.anchor: Menba‘-ı servet ikidir: Kesb, sa‘y

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Acquisition can mean obtaining wealth through work, craft, or contract, directly or indirectly, or ownership accruing over something; the latter also includes inheritance.
rows.anchor: Kesb, sa‘y ü amel, sınâat veya mukāvele ile herhangi bir cihetten bizzat veya bi’l-vâsıta istihsâldir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth here includes land, sea, and air, while mixed products are assigned to whichever of work or natural production predominates.
rows.anchor: Arz, karaya ve denize ve havaya şâmildir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Work is the nearer cause and often precedes extraction from the earth, yet depends on created faculties and resources; acquisition can never be independent, whereas the earth may be.
rows.anchor: kesb hiçbir zaman sebeb-i müstakil olamadığı hâlde arz, olabilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Workers err when they treat labor as the sole cause of wealth and capital as worthless, overlooking that labor's value is tied to the capital it produces.
rows.anchor: sa‘y ü ameli bir sebeb-i mutlak gibi telakkī etmek ve binâen‘aleyh bütün sermayeleri buna medyun farz ederek hükümsüz gibi addeylemektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Capital can facilitate and multiply later work, so hostility to it amounts to wishing for workers' own hardship and deprivation.
rows.anchor: sermâyenin gāye-i sa‘y olması ise yalnız istihlâk nokta-i nazarından değil

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Capital owners make the opposite error when they treat money as an absolute cause, disregard labor, and seek to benefit from others' work without working themselves.
rows.anchor: sermayeyi sebeb-i mutlak telakkī edip sa‘y ü ameli hükümsüz addetmektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Money in a safe feeds no one without labor; money is itself an output of past work, and exploiting labor destroys the foundation on which capitalists depend.
rows.anchor: kasalardaki paralar, kendi kendilerine hiç kimsenin karnını doyurmaz, onun bir dilim ekmek getirmesi bir amel ile mümkindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The true original capital is the earth and creation's gifts; money is only a result of labor and can serve as a means to facilitate further work.
rows.anchor: Gerçi asıl sermaye yok değildir. Fakat o olsa olsa arz ve mevâhib-i hilkattir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When money and capital become absolute rulers, workers' reaction produces conflict between labor and capital and disrupts social order.
rows.anchor: Sermaye ile sa‘y ü amel arasında cidâl başlar. Nizâm-ı cem‘iyet de muhtel olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports say some people hung date clusters in the mosque for the needy, while others brought spoiled inferior fruit thinking this was acceptable; the verse then came down.
rows.anchor: bazıları hurma salkımlarını getirirler, muhtaç olanlar yesinler diye mescide asarlardı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Obligatory dues are paid in the same class as the property: gold for gold, silver for silver, money for money, each animal kind for itself, and each crop for itself.
rows.anchor: Her malın vâcib olan vergisi kendi cinsindendir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A payer may convert lower-quality goods into the higher quality owed and pay their value at their discretion, but the due itself is not to be inferior.
rows.anchor: Bunların ednâsını a‘lâsına tahvil ederek kıymetlerini vermek mükellefin ihtiyârına aittir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Paying dues in kind is the easiest method and, by applying God's law of ease, benefited Islam's spread and the promotion of justice.
rows.anchor: dîn-i İslâm bunu emretmiş idi. Ve bunun intişâr-ı İslâm’a ve neşr-i ma‘delete pek büyük fâideleri olmuştu

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This system's public benefits depend on pious, ethical officials who guard entrusted property more carefully than their own.
rows.anchor: bunu tatbik edeceklerin Allah’ı bilir dindar, ahlâklı âmiller olması

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With trustworthy administration, much wealth can meet public needs directly and necessary exchanges can be conducted soundly, reducing expenses and expanding public resources.
rows.anchor: hem milletin mesârifi azalır hem devletin menâbi‘-i serveti inkişaf eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When officials and the public are immoral and entrusted funds are misused, concealed, stolen, or wasted, governments shift toward cash taxes; costs and burdens rise, money dominates, intermediaries profit, and producers' future is threatened.
rows.anchor: hüsn-i idare edilmeyip sû’-i isti‘mâl, ketm, sirkat, israf, lâubâlîlik meydan almış bulunursa

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mismanagement and lack of religious duty cause social calamity; those who reject this divine command act against wisdom and ruin their future however learned they claim to be.
rows.anchor: insanların dîn ü diyânetten kaçınmaları ve infak vazifelerini hüsn-i suretle îfâ ve bunları hüsn-i idare etmemeleri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruling's scope over voluntary charity is debated: unlawful wealth cannot be given voluntarily for divine reward, though inferior-quality lawful wealth may be given.
rows.anchor: Doğrusu haramdan nâfile sadaka da câiz olmaz. ‘İndallah sevâbı olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition is binding in obligatory dues and expresses dislike, whether prohibitive or mild, in voluntary gifts; its general force includes both.
rows.anchor: Hükm-i umûmîsi tahrîmen veya tenzîhen kerâhet demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse appears to cover all wealth but leaves the threshold, amount, and scope by property class unspecified; Prophetic practice and hadith clarify these, with details left to legal manuals.
rows.anchor: Âyetin zâhiri her nevi maldan bir zekât lâzım geleceğini gösteriyor gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God commands spending from pure earnings and produce rather than inferior goods one would refuse oneself.
rows.anchor: Sizin kazandıklarınızın ve bizim yerden çıkardıklarımızın temizlerinden infak ediniz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is self-sufficient, so charity benefits its giver; as Praiseworthy, He also rewards good works with greater favor and appreciates efforts made for Him.
rows.anchor: Diğer bir mâna ile: Allah hamîddir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan may be the despairing Iblis, any devilish whisperer, or the commanding self; he frightens people with poverty and urges stinginess and spending on sins and base desires.
rows.anchor: O şeytan, rahmet-i ilâhiyeden ümîdini kesmiş olan o me’yus İblis veya hayır işlere karşı gizliden veya açıktan ümitsizlik telkin ederek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises forgiveness for sins, multiplied replacement for worldly spending, and happiness and reward in both worlds.
rows.anchor: kat kat kârlar, dünya ve âhirette ecr ü mesûbât ile yüksek saadetler temin eyliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's bounty is abundant and His knowledge is complete, so He knows the value of each gift, rewards it, and is not constrained in fulfilling His promise.
rows.anchor: Her şeyin önünü sonunu bilerek emr ü vaad eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives wisdom to whomever He wills without restriction, since He is all-encompassing.
rows.anchor: her kime dilerse hikmet verir, vermek için hiçbir kayd ile mukayyed olmaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can grant rational people the authority to prevent harm and secure benefit, true knowledge, right choice, and beneficial agency.
rows.anchor: Men‘-i mefsedet ve celb-i maslahat edecek sebebiyet ve hâkimiyeti, ilm-i hak ve bi’l-irâde fi‘l-i savâb ile âlimiyyet-i fâile ve fâiliyyet-i nâfi‘ayı

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On Yaqub's reading, with kasra on the tā, the phrase can mean whomever God gives wisdom.
rows.anchor: yahut -“tâ”nın kesriyle Ya‘kūb kıraati üzere- her kime hikmet

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever receives wisdom receives abundant good: with wisdom one can reach thousands of goods, and wisdom encompasses the good of both worlds, while unwisdom's gains are unstable.
rows.anchor: hikmetsiz binde bir hayra erilirse, bir hikmet ile binlerle hayra erilir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only people with sound minds reflect and accept reminders; those who fail to do so cannot benefit from divine wisdom even when signs remind them.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ âyâtıyla ihtar ve tezkir eder de yine tezekkür etmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Receiving wisdom requires the servant's receptivity as well as God's gift; clean reason, a clean heart, and reflection are prerequisites.
rows.anchor: Demek ki hikmete ermek için vermek kâfî değil, almak da lâzımdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those captive to desire and Satan cannot reflect on inner or outer signs, select truth and good from what they recall, or walk the path of wisdom.
rows.anchor: Allah’ın verdiği aklı şehevâta ve şeytanın vesveselerine kaptıranlar ne vâridât-ı enfüsiyeyi, ne de mevârid-i âfâkiyeyi tezekkür ve tefekkür edemezler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The initial conditions for wisdom are gifts of prior divine will, while its effects unfold through human will accompanied by divine will; human will is a customary cause and God's will the effective cause.
rows.anchor: Meşiyyet-i abd sebeb-i âdî, meşiyyet-i ilâhiye illet-i mûcibedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nothing exists without God's will; human will is an intermediary, and wisdom's essence is bestowed while its effects are both earned and bestowed.
rows.anchor: asl-ı hikmet mevhub ve âsâr-ı hikmet meksub ve mevhubdur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word hikmah relates to judgment, governance, and making firm; because it has several related uses, its meaning must be read from context.
rows.anchor: Bu kelime hüküm, hükûmet, ihkâm mânalarıyla alâkadar olarak masdar ve isim olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As a verbal noun, wisdom fundamentally means preventing corruption and bringing rectitude; judgment and firmness derive from that root.
rows.anchor: esasında men‘-i fesad ve celb-i salâh mânası vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom can name a thing's intended benefit or consequence; it is narrower than general benefit, broader than a final cause, and expresses ordered causal relations.
rows.anchor: hikmet, “fâide”den ehas ve “illet-i gāiye”den e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In its broadest use wisdom names every good science and righteous act that brings benefit, welfare, or soundness, with practical knowledge and action especially central.
rows.anchor: En umûmî olarak hikmet, menfaat ve maslahat ve ihkâm mânası dolayısıyla her ilm-i hasen ve amel-i sâlihin ismidir

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: One definition of wisdom is correctness in both speech and action, transmitted from Mujahid by Ibn Abi Najih.
rows.anchor: Kavilde ve fiilde isabet (Mücâhid’den İbn Ebî Necîh

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Speech and action both matter: speech is correct when it matches truth and reality, while action must accord with sound judgment and achieve its beneficial purpose.
rows.anchor: Kavilde isabet hakka, fiilde isabet hayra müteveccihdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom unites knowledge of truth at its beginning with good action at its end; neither correct speech alone nor correct action alone suffices.
rows.anchor: Hakīkat-i hikmet evvelinden ilmî, âhirinden amelî iki haysiyetin ictimâ‘ı demektir

rows.speaker: Mukātil ve İbn Kuteybe
rows.claim: A second definition makes wisdom the union of knowledge and practice; someone who cannot combine both is not wise.
rows.anchor: Hikmet ilim ve ameldir: İlim ve onunla ameldir. Bu ikisini cem‘edemeyene

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here knowledge means certainty and is firm when certain; practice is firm when it hits its purpose, combining tested practical knowledge with action that witnesses to knowledge.
rows.anchor: ilmin muhkemliği yakīniyetinde, amelin muhkemliği gayesine hakkıyla isabetindedir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wisdom is knowledge and will proportionately expressed in purposeful action, or, in another formulation, the combination of science and craft.
rows.anchor: Hâsılı hikmet, ilim ile iradenin mütenâsiben fiile çıkması

rows.speaker: Mücâhid
rows.claim: Mujahid gives a third definition: wisdom is knowledge and fiqh.
rows.anchor: Hikmet: İlim ve fıkıh demektir (Mücâhid)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fiqh is close to a synonym for wisdom: it grasps purposes, detailed causes, and useful action, especially the aims, duties, rights, benefits, and harms of religion.
rows.anchor: “Fıkıh” kelimesi esas itibariyle “hikmet” kelimesine

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A scholar without fiqh cannot be wise, but fiqh alone is not enough either, since it depends on the methods and other sciences needed to establish it.
rows.anchor: fıkhı olmayan ne kadar âlim olursa olsun hakîm olamaz

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If knowledge means foundational theology and fiqh means practical branches, wisdom combines theoretical and practical understanding and acting accordingly.
rows.anchor: hikmet usûl ve fürû‘u, mebâdî ve makāsıdı hakāyık u dekāyıkıyla bilip yapacağını tâyin ve muktezâsıyla amel etmek

rows.speaker: İbrâhim Neha‘î
rows.claim: A fourth definition describes wisdom as knowing and understanding the meanings of things.
rows.anchor: Hikmet; me‘ânî-i eşyâyı mârifet ve fehmdir (İbrâhim Neha‘î)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here meanings include effective qualities, causes, and purposes: wisdom follows causal order to understand the essences and ends of things.
rows.anchor: eşyâ beynindeki nizâm-ı illiyeti tâkip ile mâhiyyât ve gāyât-ı eşyâyı fehm eylemek

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This definition omits action and so is broader than earlier ones in one respect, but its restriction to all meanings of things makes it narrower in another.
rows.anchor: amel kaydını hazf etmiş ve hikmeti yalnız ilmî haysiyetle almış olduğundan evvelkilerden e‘amdır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Understanding means grasping a thing's intellectual form; not all knowledge is wisdom, and adding actual action would wrongly require a wise person to be able to make everything.
rows.anchor: Fehm ise bir şeyin sûret-i akliyesini kavramaktır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This definition avoids attributing human-style cognition to God, since ma'rifa and understanding imply prior ignorance; it also matches a comprehensive science that unifies disciplines.
rows.anchor: Zira ilm-i ilâhîye fıkıh denilmediği gibi mârifet ve fehm de denilmez

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although such comprehensive understanding may seem impossible for humans, it is possible as a faculty or near capacity, and through God's will it may occur in prophets and great saints.
rows.anchor: böyle bir ilm-i hikmet mümkin midir? Evvelâ marifet ve fehm bilfiil değil meleke ve kuvve-i karîbe mânasına olunca mümkin ve vâki‘dir

rows.speaker: Süddî
rows.claim: Al-Suddi interprets wisdom in this verse as prophethood, the highest bestowed wisdom because it combines knowledge and action.
rows.anchor: Süddî bu âyette de böyle tefsir etmiştir

rows.speaker: İbn Rüşd
rows.claim: Ibn Rushd acknowledges this account of wisdom in the Tahafut: every prophet is wise, though not every wise person is a prophet.
rows.anchor: İbn Rüşd Tehâfüt’ünde “Her nebî hakîmdir, fakat her hakîm nebî değildir”

rows.speaker: Zeyd b. Eslem ve oğlu
rows.claim: A fifth definition calls wisdom intelligence concerning God's command; intellect here is broad but does not itself include action.
rows.anchor: Zeyd b. Eslem ve oğlu

rows.speaker: Şüreyk
rows.claim: A sixth definition makes wisdom understanding; the author says its broadest cognitive sense is actual understanding, not merely the faculty of understanding, and both are divine gifts.
rows.anchor: Hikmet, fehm demektir (Şüreyk)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mu'tazilites take understanding as a faculty, but the author prefers actual understanding; without understanding, a person cannot be wise.
rows.anchor: Mutezile bunu kuvve-i fehmiyye mânasında ahz etmişlerse de doğrusu fiilen fehmdir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The last three definitions consider only wisdom's cognitive aspect, while other definitions consider only its practical aspect.
rows.anchor: Bu üç tarif, hikmeti yalnız haysiyet-i ilmiyesiyle mülâhaza etmiştir
